programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean air am beò-ghlacadh leis a' bhurras bheag. Ach càite an deach e? Daolag-bhreac and Seillean are fascinated with the little caterpillar. But where did he go?

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona a' cur seachad an latha a' leantainn na faoileagan 's ag ionnsachadh ioma rud inntinneach mun na cleachdaidhean aca... fiosrachadh a tha air leth feumail nuair a thig Baba bochd a chur ann an cunnart! Oona spends the day following the seagulls, learning all sorts of interesting facts about their behaviour. This information comes in very useful when Baba gets himself in a spot of bother!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha tubaist aig Bernie a tha fàgail an t-slige aige briste! Tha Oona 's Silky a' cur romhpa slige ùr a lorg dha aig grunnd na mara ach chan e gnìomh furasta a th' ann dhaibh tè fhreagarrach fhaighinn! When Bernie has an accident and manages to break his shell, Oona and Silky volunteer to dive to the depths to find him a new one. However, it proves to be quite the challenge to find one suitable.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha damhan-allaidh beag snog san t-sionc’. Tha Fuigheag ‘son cluich leis ach tha Boban caran eagalach bhuaithe. Saoil am faigh Boban seachad air an eagal? There’s a cute little spider inside the sink. Fuigheag wants to play with it but Boban is a little scared of it. Will Boban get over this fear?

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha Sif, Pipp is Bran a’ peantadh le mil, flùr-bhileagan dathte agus seann bhogsa piotsa! Ziff, Pipp and Button become painters using honey, colourful petals and an old pizza box!

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: An-diugh tha Fionnlagh agus Scott còmhla rithe ‘s iad a’ dèanamh pizzathan le tomàtothan agus brocail. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad a bhith cinnteach gu bheil an stuth a tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a thathar a’ fàs thomàtothan. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson na pizzathan ullachadh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd gan ithe. Linda Macleod is joined by Finlay and Scott to make tomato and broccoli pizza. But before they start cooking, they have to ensure they have all the ingredients. If not, they make a list and go shopping. They also learn more about how tomatoes are grown, then return to the kitchen to make the pizzas before sitting down to tuck in.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Catriona Mhoireach a’ leughadh An Solas air an Oidhche. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh ’s a dhealbhachadh le Marie Voight agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. Catriona Murray reads An Solas air an Oidhche, written and illustrated by Marie Voight and translated into Gaelic by Donald John Macleod.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha iomagain air an Rìgh ’son ’s gum bi Stella sàbhailt' nuair a thèid i a-mach aig meadhan-oidhch’ 'son an dùbhradh-gealaich fhaicinn. The King is worried for Stella’s safety when she goes out at midnight to see the lunar eclipse.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella air a gealladh a thoirt gun toir i taic le bhith coimhead às dèidh na piseig' ùr aig Mìcheal. Tha aice ri bhith sèolta ge-tà oir tha fios aice nach bi an Rìgh toilichte le seo seach gu bheil i fhèin ‘s e fhèin aileirdsig o chait. Stella has promised to help look after Mìcheal’s new kitten. She has to be cunning though as she knows the King won’t be happy - she and the King are both allergic to cats.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha sgrudaire sgoile air nochdadh aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche agus chan eil Maighstir Mackle neo na tidsearan deiseil air a shon. Chan eil cùisean a’ coimhead ro mhath do Mhaighstir MhicFhraing ach tha Maighstir Strachan air a chasan, neo co-dhiù aona chois a lorg. Dè as urrainn a dhol ceàrr?! There’s a surprise visit from a school inspector at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche. It’s not looking good for Mr MacFhraing, although Mr Strachan seems to have found his feet, well one foot at least. What could possibly go wrong?!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Troig air misean oir tha e air ròghnachadh clàr a bhriseadh is ainm fhaighinn dhan Ghumbaldeacs. Airson sin a dhèanamh, feumaidh e sia gaoisidean sròine a shlaodadh a-mach à sianar Bhògais. Ach ciamar a thèid dha? Troig is on a mission as he has decided that he must break a record and get his name into the Gumbledex. To achieve this, he must pull six nasal hairs out of six Bògaisean. How will he get on?

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Bonns air proipeilear Shona a bhriseadh, tha i ga chleith bhuaithe, ’s tha i fhèin, Uilidh is Troig a’ dèanamh air Cnoc Bògais airson pàirt ùr a lorg airson am proipeilear a chàradh. Saoil ciamar a thèid leotha? When Bonns breaks Sona’s propeller, she doesn’t tell him. Instead she goes off to Cnoc Bògais with Uilidh and Troig in search of a replacement part. How they will get on?

programme.title: Eilean Mo Ghaoil (From Lewis with Love)
programme.desc: It’s harvest time at Bragar machair, children try their hand at rowing in Shawbost, and RSPB warden Shona helps protect an endangered summer visitor to the island.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na ciad ceumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Coinnichidh sinn ris an neach-ionnsachaidh Frances Knows, agus tha Calum MacIlleathain a’ gabhail turas bàta air Linne Chrombaigh agus e an tòir air leumadairean-mara. Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne: www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan a tha ri fhaighinn air BBC Sounds. Joy Dunlop meets learner Frances Knows and Calum Maclean is in his element as he takes a trip on the Cromarty Firth in search of dolphins. Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay MacMahon walks with Calum Steele through the Perthshire countryside, along a reservoir and to the top of Innerdownie. He talks about family life and the importance his father had on him and the community. As they appreciate the nature surrounding them and discuss why they love the Scottish outdoors, Calum also reflects on his long career as a police officer and as general secretary of the Scottish Police Federation. Tha Ramsay a’ coiseachd tro dhùthaich Shiorrachd Pheairt, an cois tasgadh-uisge agus gu mullach Inbhir Dùnaigh cuide ri Calum Steele. Tha e a’ bruidhinn mu a bheatha teaghlaich agus a’ bhuaidh mhòr a bh’ aig athair air fhèin agus air a’ choimhearsnachd. A’ gabhail a-steach an àrainneachd nàdarrach mu thimcheall orra agus a’ bruidhinn mun ùidh a th’ aig an dithis ann a bhith a-muigh ann an Alba, tha Calum cuideachd a’ cnuasachdh air a dhreuchd fhada mar oifigear poilis agus mar Àrd-Rùnaire de Chaidreachas Poileas na h-Alba. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Airson a’ chiad uair, tha pàrtaidhean nàiseantach a-nis a’ riaghladh ann an Alba agus ‘sa Chuimrigh, is tha Prìomh Mhinistear Nàiseantach ann an Èirinn a Tuath. Tha Mìcheal MacNèill air a bhith ‘sna trì dùthchannan a’ coinneachdadh ri daoine air gach taobh de dheasbad na bunreachd. For the first time, nationalist parties lead the governments of Scotland and Wales, while Northern Ireland has a nationalist First Minister. Join Michael MacNeil as he travels through the three nations, meeting those on both sides of the constitutional divide.

programme.title: Cuirm aig Celtic
programme.desc: Ceòl is còmhradh bho chuirm shònraichte le Bon Débarras. À Montreal, bha an còmhlan ann an Glaschu aig Celtic Connections 2026 airson consairt sònraichte le Sian. Freumhaichte ann an ceòl traidiseanta Quebec le measgachadh de cheòl, dannsa is bàrdachd, bha spionnadh am pailteas aca gus cùisean a chuir air a chasan aig Barony Hall. Air a lìbhrigeadh le Megan NicGill-Fhaolain. Music and conversation from a concert by Montreal band Bon Débarras. They were in Glasgow as part of Celtic Connections 2026 for a special performance alongside Sian. Rooted in the traditional music of Quebec, their sound is a fusion of music, dance and poetry and they brought an incredible energy to kick off proceedings at The Barony Hall. Presented by Megan MacLellan. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd inntinneach nam muilnean tro na bliadhnaichean. The story of island mills throughout the years.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Music documentary in which Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh explore shared musical roots in Connemara.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc: Tha tairgse tharraingeach air tighinn bho Lewis Friseal. Feumaidh a’ chlann-nighean còmhradh mu bhith a’ reic a’ ghnothachais ach aig an dearbh àm seo chan eil iad a’ bruidhinn ri chèile. Tha sùil Katie air mogan airgid. Tha Angela a’ bruadar mu ghaol fad-astarach. Tha Daniel a’ cur seachad a shaoghal aig obair far a a bheil peinnseanairean le eòlas a’ tabhann comhairle àraid. Tha Betty a’ nochdadh dreach ùr, dàn airson sèisean coimhead nan eun. An dàrna sreath den chomadaidh magaidh-aithriseach le Hannah McKirdy agus Lana Pheutan mar chleasaichean agus sgrìobhaichean. A tempting offer from Lewis Fraser is on the table. The girls need to discuss selling the business, but right now they aren’t speaking to each other. Katie sees pound signs. Angela’s dreaming of long-distance love. Daniel spends all his time at work, where some experienced OAPs offer some choice romance advice. Betty unveils a bold new look for birdwatching season. Series two of the popular mockumentary comedy written by and starring Hannah McKirdy and Lana Pheutan. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: The Lark Ascending
programme.desc: Dame Diana Rigg explores the enduring popularity of The Lark Ascending by the English composer Ralph Vaughan Williams, which was recently voted Britain's favourite piece of classical music by listeners to Desert Island Discs on BBC Radio 4. Composed at a key turning point in world history, The Lark Ascending represents music for all occasions. It is used in rites of passage such as births, deaths and marriages, and is a favourite for film-makers looking to create that quintessential English pastoral feel. Fans of the work include actor Peter Sallis, who wants a copy of The Lark Ascending to be buried with him, top violinist Tasmin Little, who has played the piece as part of the BBC Proms, and music critic Michael Kennedy, who was a personal friend of Vaughan Williams. The programme includes a beautiful new performance of the work in the same village hall where it was heard for the first time in December 1920. The Lark Ascending is performed by 15-year-old violin prodigy Julia Hwang and pianist Charles Matthews, using the original arrangement for violin and piano.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo joins Navy Wings pilots for a spectacular close formation flight in the skies over Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton. He also visits the magnificent Elizabethan mansion of Longleat, seat of the Marquesses of Bath, to find out about the estate’s remarkable survival after the Second World War. At Chippenham in Wiltshire, Michael pays a call on a signalling manufacturer that has been at the heart of British railway projects for decades and has a go on the centre’s simulator, driving the Elizabeth Line train to Paddington.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches England’s south coast to continue his exploration of postwar Britain. He begins in Dorset on the Swanage Railway, riding a glorious 1940s steam locomotive on the trail of one of Britain’s most popular children’s authors, Enid Blyton. In Poole, Michael discovers an icon of the Swinging Sixties – the lava lamp, invented in the town by an eccentric accountant. At Romsey, Michael heads to the magnificent Broadlands Estate, once home of Louis Mountbatten, first Earl Mountbatten of Burma. Michael’s last stop on this leg of the journey is Portchester, on the northern edge of Portsmouth Harbour, where he visits a factory manufacturing a marine craft pioneered in the 1950s – the hovercraft.

programme.title: Wild
programme.desc: Wildlife cameraman Gordon Buchanan explores his native Mull and some of the nearby islands, filming otters, deer, puffins, seals and a minke whale.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the surprising roots of Greek art, beginning his journey in Crete at the palace of Knossos, legendary home of the Minotaur. He travels to Santorini to the 'Greek Pompeii' and finds gold in the fabled stronghold of Mycenae and dazzling remains from Greece's Dark Ages. Alastair discovers the beginnings of a defining spirit in Greek art, embracing mythology, a passion for symmetry and an obsession with the human body.

programme.title: Andy Warhol's America
programme.desc: The final episode sees a much more cautious Warhol: a man obsessed with money and security as he reflects on the upper echelons of American society, drag queens and racism.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Could alien life exist closer than we think - perhaps right next door? The team investigate evidence that suggests the search for life beyond Earth may lie within our own solar system.

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes focuses on work that responded to the Vietnam War and civil strife. He traces the development of minimalism and ends up on top of an extinct volcano.

programme.title: Stolen: Catching the Art Thieves
programme.desc: This episode looks at the theft of a self-portrait of Rembrandt in a brutal robbery in Stockholm and hears from the investigators leading a complex hunt from Russian organised crime to America. The investigation takes a surprising twist involving charismatic FBI agents operating in Hollywood.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the surprising roots of Greek art, beginning his journey in Crete at the palace of Knossos, legendary home of the Minotaur. He travels to Santorini to the 'Greek Pompeii' and finds gold in the fabled stronghold of Mycenae and dazzling remains from Greece's Dark Ages. Alastair discovers the beginnings of a defining spirit in Greek art, embracing mythology, a passion for symmetry and an obsession with the human body.

programme.title: The Lark Ascending
programme.desc: Dame Diana Rigg explores the enduring popularity of The Lark Ascending by the English composer Ralph Vaughan Williams, which was recently voted Britain's favourite piece of classical music by listeners to Desert Island Discs on BBC Radio 4. Composed at a key turning point in world history, The Lark Ascending represents music for all occasions. It is used in rites of passage such as births, deaths and marriages, and is a favourite for film-makers looking to create that quintessential English pastoral feel. Fans of the work include actor Peter Sallis, who wants a copy of The Lark Ascending to be buried with him, top violinist Tasmin Little, who has played the piece as part of the BBC Proms, and music critic Michael Kennedy, who was a personal friend of Vaughan Williams. The programme includes a beautiful new performance of the work in the same village hall where it was heard for the first time in December 1920. The Lark Ascending is performed by 15-year-old violin prodigy Julia Hwang and pianist Charles Matthews, using the original arrangement for violin and piano.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo joins Navy Wings pilots for a spectacular close formation flight in the skies over Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton. He also visits the magnificent Elizabethan mansion of Longleat, seat of the Marquesses of Bath, to find out about the estate’s remarkable survival after the Second World War. At Chippenham in Wiltshire, Michael pays a call on a signalling manufacturer that has been at the heart of British railway projects for decades and has a go on the centre’s simulator, driving the Elizabeth Line train to Paddington.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches England’s south coast to continue his exploration of postwar Britain. He begins in Dorset on the Swanage Railway, riding a glorious 1940s steam locomotive on the trail of one of Britain’s most popular children’s authors, Enid Blyton. In Poole, Michael discovers an icon of the Swinging Sixties – the lava lamp, invented in the town by an eccentric accountant. At Romsey, Michael heads to the magnificent Broadlands Estate, once home of Louis Mountbatten, first Earl Mountbatten of Burma. Michael’s last stop on this leg of the journey is Portchester, on the northern edge of Portsmouth Harbour, where he visits a factory manufacturing a marine craft pioneered in the 1950s – the hovercraft.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s chocks away as Christina Trevanion pilots a special episode all about aviation. Among the historic aircraft of the Royal Airforce Museum London, Christina rounds up some deals that really took off at auction and others that had a bumpy ride. In Ardingly, a former flying ace and his daughter plan to soar to victory when they go shopping with Nick Hall, while in Newark, university friends Joel and Oscar hope to land a good deal with a propeller made into a coat rack, until their expert Catherine Southon grounds the idea. In Hendon, Christina learns about the history and heroism of the pilots who flew some of the 74 aircraft on display, and in Bristol, Eric Knowles reminisces about the glamour of supersonic travel from the luxurious interior of a surviving Concorde jet. Meanwhile, Natasha Raskin Sharp is flying high in a far older plane – a restored World War II Spitfire.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: For decades, Dubai has sold itself as a safe place to live, do business and party. But when war broke out in nearby Iran, the city’s carefully curated image was shattered. Missiles and drones hit luxury hotels and critical infrastructure, expats scrambled for safety, and the government clamped down on sharing images of the war. Panorama reveals through the eyes of British residents, business owners and experts how Dubai’s promise of security and prosperity has been tested like never before.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international, and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth. Leah has aspirations to rear some animals in their new country pad, so Nicki takes the couple to a micro animal park to meet a selection of adorable farmyard friends, including a donkey that likes to dress up and a piano-playing pig!

programme.title: Cowboys & Aliens
programme.desc: Jake Lonergan wakes up in the desert with no memory of who he is or how he got there. But in the nearby town of Absolution, he's a wanted man, and Jake is arrested for being one of the most feared gunslingers in the Wild West, and the leader of the Lonergan gang. When the town comes under attack by mysterious craft that kidnap people off the streets, including the sheriff, the tough and feared Colonel Dolarhyde puts together a posse to find all the victims, including his kidnapped son. Mistrusted and feared by the others, Lonergan joins the posse and sets out to get justice.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s chocks away as Christina Trevanion pilots a special episode all about aviation. Among the historic aircraft of the Royal Airforce Museum London, Christina rounds up some deals that really took off at auction and others that had a bumpy ride. In Ardingly, a former flying ace and his daughter plan to soar to victory when they go shopping with Nick Hall, while in Newark, university friends Joel and Oscar hope to land a good deal with a propeller made into a coat rack, until their expert Catherine Southon grounds the idea. In Hendon, Christina learns about the history and heroism of the pilots who flew some of the 74 aircraft on display, and in Bristol, Eric Knowles reminisces about the glamour of supersonic travel from the luxurious interior of a surviving Concorde jet. Meanwhile, Natasha Raskin Sharp is flying high in a far older plane – a restored World War II Spitfire.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof

programme.title: Expert Witness

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A tiger in a north London maisonette has Owain earning his stripes. Don’t panic, it’s not a real one! Meanwhile, Dion is dealing with damp in Kidsgrove, and Martel is in Hartlepool, where a two-bedroom mid-terrace has an intriguingly low guide price.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s chocks away as Christina Trevanion pilots a special episode all about aviation. Among the historic aircraft of the Royal Airforce Museum London, Christina rounds up some deals that really took off at auction and others that had a bumpy ride. In Ardingly, a former flying ace and his daughter plan to soar to victory when they go shopping with Nick Hall, while in Newark, university friends Joel and Oscar hope to land a good deal with a propeller made into a coat rack, until their expert Catherine Southon grounds the idea. In Hendon, Christina learns about the history and heroism of the pilots who flew some of the 74 aircraft on display, and in Bristol, Eric Knowles reminisces about the glamour of supersonic travel from the luxurious interior of a surviving Concorde jet. Meanwhile, Natasha Raskin Sharp is flying high in a far older plane – a restored World War II Spitfire.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: For decades, Dubai has sold itself as a safe place to live, do business and party. But when war broke out in nearby Iran, the city’s carefully curated image was shattered. Missiles and drones hit luxury hotels and critical infrastructure, expats scrambled for safety, and the government clamped down on sharing images of the war. Panorama reveals through the eyes of British residents, business owners and experts how Dubai’s promise of security and prosperity has been tested like never before.

programme.title: Barra's Return of the Wild
programme.desc: By the middle of this century, it’s predicted more than two-thirds of the world’s population will be living in urban areas. BBC weather presenter Barra Best visits cities across Europe to meet the people at the forefront of wildlife conservation. He finds how their ingenuity in providing safe spaces for plants and animals in urban environments is helping reverse declining trends and seeing species return to places where they’d been wiped out by development. Beginning his journey in his hometown of Belfast, Barra finds out how a lightbulb moment saved one of the city’s most spectacular natural phenomena from extinction. He travels to the Balearic island of Ibiza, where work is underway to protect their national symbol from an invading snake. We see how one woman is single-handedly protecting the fish in the canals of Leiden in the Netherlands, and meet the hedgehog researchers in Berlin hoping to solve a prickly problem. In Cork, we meet the team giving the city’s growing population of peregrine falcons a safe space high above the city. A Eurovision Co-Production.

Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth. Leah has aspirations to rear some animals in their new country pad, so Nicki takes the couple to a micro animal park to meet a selection of adorable farmyard friends, including a donkey that likes to dress up and a piano-playing pig!

programme.title: Cowboys & Aliens
programme.desc: Jake Lonergan wakes up in the desert with no memory of who he is or how he got there. But in the nearby town of Absolution, he's a wanted man, and Jake is arrested for being one of the most feared gunslingers in the Wild West, and the leader of the Lonergan gang. When the town comes under attack by mysterious craft that kidnap people off the streets, including the sheriff, the tough and feared Colonel Dolarhyde puts together a posse to find all the victims, including his kidnapped son. Mistrusted and feared by the others, Lonergan joins the posse and sets out to get justice.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s chocks away as Christina Trevanion pilots a special episode all about aviation. Among the historic aircraft of the Royal Airforce Museum London, Christina rounds up some deals that really took off at auction and others that had a bumpy ride. In Ardingly, a former flying ace and his daughter plan to soar to victory when they go shopping with Nick Hall, while in Newark, university friends Joel and Oscar hope to land a good deal with a propeller made into a coat rack, until their expert Catherine Southon grounds the idea. In Hendon, Christina learns about the history and heroism of the pilots who flew some of the 74 aircraft on display, and in Bristol, Eric Knowles reminisces about the glamour of supersonic travel from the luxurious interior of a surviving Concorde jet. programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: This documentary follows Joe and her remarkable junior team at Mynydd Sleddog Adventures as they fight for qualification to represent Great Britain at the sled dog racing European championships in Sweden. They have qualified previously, but couldn’t attend due to the high cost of travelling to North America. Now, with a new season ahead, the stakes are higher, the pressure is heavier, and the dream feels both closer and more fragile than ever. As we follow them through wild weather, school commitments, long travel days and early starts, what unfolds is the story of a group of young people who refuse to let circumstance dictate the limits of their ambition. These are working-class kids from rural Wales finding purpose, confidence and identity through an unconventional sport, and forging deep bonds with their dogs along the way. The film builds towards the pivotal moment of qualification in Scotland: a second chance at the world stage. Whether they make it or fall short, it’s a story about grit, community and daring to believe that extraordinary dreams can come from the most unexpected places.

Among the historic aircraft of the Royal Airforce Museum London, Christina rounds up some deals that really took off at auction and others that had a bumpy ride. In Ardingly, a former flying ace and his daughter plan to soar to victory when they go shopping with Nick Hall, while in Newark, university friends Joel and Oscar hope to land a good deal with a propeller made into a coat rack, until their expert Catherine Southon grounds the idea. In Hendon, Christina learns about the history and heroism of the pilots who flew some of the 74 aircraft on display, and in Bristol, Eric Knowles reminisces about the glamour of supersonic travel from the luxurious interior of a surviving Concorde jet. Meanwhile, Natasha Raskin Sharp is flying high in a far older plane – a restored World War II Spitfire.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Cowboys & Aliens
programme.desc: Jake Lonergan wakes up in the desert with no memory of who he is or how he got there. But in the nearby town of Absolution, he's a wanted man, and Jake is arrested for being one of the most feared gunslingers in the Wild West, and the leader of the Lonergan gang. When the town comes under attack by mysterious craft that kidnap people off the streets, including the sheriff, the tough and feared Colonel Dolarhyde puts together a posse to find all the victims, including his kidnapped son. Mistrusted and feared by the others, Lonergan joins the posse and sets out to get justice.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

Panorama reveals through the eyes of British residents, business owners and experts how Dubai’s promise of security and prosperity has been tested like never before.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international, and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth. Leah has aspirations to rear some animals in their new country pad, so Nicki takes the couple to a micro animal park to meet a selection of adorable farmyard friends, including a donkey that likes to dress up and a piano-playing pig!

programme.title: Cowboys & Aliens
programme.desc: Jake Lonergan wakes up in the desert with no memory of who he is or how he got there. But in the nearby town of Absolution, he's a wanted man, and Jake is arrested for being one of the most feared gunslingers in the Wild West, and the leader of the Lonergan gang. When the town comes under attack by mysterious craft that kidnap people off the streets, including the sheriff, the tough and feared Colonel Dolarhyde puts together a posse to find all the victims, including his kidnapped son. Mistrusted and feared by the others, Lonergan joins the posse and sets out to get justice.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: A reclusive millionaire is found murdered in his home in west London, and police find hundreds of thousands of pounds in cash there. Why haven’t his killers taken the money? Only old-fashioned detective work can find them, but they’ve fled abroad. Also, a heavily pregnant woman is kidnapped and assaulted, but it’s not until the offender is arrested elsewhere for a lesser crime that police are able to connect him.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: Forensic explosives experts are tasked with examining the crime scenes after the London bombings to establish if the devices had the signature of any known terrorist organisation.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A tiger in a north London maisonette has Owain earning his stripes. Don’t panic, it’s not a real one! Meanwhile, Dion is dealing with damp in Kidsgrove, and Martel is in Hartlepool, where a two-bedroom mid-terrace has an intriguingly low guide price.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s chocks away as Christina Trevanion pilots a special episode all about aviation. Among the historic aircraft of the Royal Airforce Museum London, Christina rounds up some deals that really took off at auction and others that had a bumpy ride. In Ardingly, a former flying ace and his daughter plan to soar to victory when they go shopping with Nick Hall, while in Newark, university friends Joel and Oscar hope to land a good deal with a propeller made into a coat rack, until their expert Catherine Southon grounds the idea. In Hendon, Christina learns about the history and heroism of the pilots who flew some of the 74 aircraft on display, and in Bristol, Eric Knowles reminisces about the glamour of supersonic travel from the luxurious interior of a surviving Concorde jet. Meanwhile, Natasha Raskin Sharp is flying high in a far older plane – a restored World War II Spitfire.

programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Chef Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond are on a mission to highlight the fantastic range of great produce Scotland has to offer. This week they’re focusing on fish, cooking a fish pie with mussels, haddock, plaice and smoked salmon. Joining them in the kitchen are fish supplier Fiona Houston and food and drink journalist Rosalind Erskine, who mixes an Angus breakfast martini using local gin infused with marmalade.

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: Cairngorm is at the heart of Scotland's greatest winter wilderness. As the first storms of the winter blow in, the ski patrol is working hard to get the resort open as early as possible. Spud the piper plays at a fairy-tale castle, and at La Taverna, Toni rips out a historic bar.

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: Cairngorm is at the heart of Scotland's greatest winter wilderness. Christmas is coming and the reindeer are being prepared for their busiest day of the year. The ski patrol gets some avalanche training with the help of the RAF, and a massive snow gun arrives on the mountain as the weather gods get fickle.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The nine designers storm a medieval-style castle to turn hotel bedrooms into perfect love nests as they draw on their own ideas of what makes a romantic retreat for inspiration. They are able to reuse and repurpose the hotel’s existing furniture to show off their ability to upcycle and demonstrate their styling skills, before they are judged by Michelle and hotel design expert Linda Boronkay.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: Desperate to stop Mikey from speaking to the press, Gillian’s meddling backfires disastrously. Meanwhile, Lenny’s suspicions over Lydia’s behaviour sparks a shock revelation, Viv expands her web of lies to get Alex onside, and Nicole’s recent blackmail plans are thwarted once again.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Alan’s off out, and Michelle has invited Beth, Cathy and Christine over for a Girls’ Night. Cathy sets the tone by downing shots, and the revelations soon flow about the annoying things their men do. But when Beth jokes about one of Christine’s annoying habits, Christine gets the hump. It takes Michelle and a negotiation over a cheese toastie for Christine to forgive Beth. With the tunes now on, the dancing begins, and for a moment it seems as though nothing could come between these women. They even get a bit emotional. And when the girls decide to watch a film, Cathy jumps in with the suggestion they stick on a porno.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Mrs Brown becomes a podcast sensation – without even leaving the house. Cathy is horrified to discover her mother has accidentally hijacked her new podcast project. Guest-starring Simon Delaney.

programme.title: Janey and Ashley Get a Real Job
programme.desc: It turns out that Janey and Ashley fight every time they are together on a flight - so will sparks fly as they try out three very different jobs in an airport? Customer service, attention to detail and following instructions are essential when checking people in, baggage handling and working as part of the airport’s fire service. However, there is a lot to remember and absolutely no room for error, not to mention the challenge of fighting a fire on a fuselage. Can Ashley and Janey impress their boss and keep to the schedule? And which one will win the ‘best employee’ trophy?

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: In Fife, Andy and Jo prepare to compete at one of the biggest highlights in the farming calendar, the Royal Highland Show. The event holds a special place in their hearts, as it's where they first met, but this year it's all about who can win the first rosette. In Caithness, it’s shearing time for Sally and champion shearer Helga. Long-time friends, the two women have competed together in New Zealand. Things are a lot trickier now with children in the mix as they wrestle sheep while trying to keep the kids amused. At Hillhead Farm, the first event of the season is imminent. The whole family pitches in to get the marquee up and the event site finished, and a decision has been made that will affect Ben’s future on the farm.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Calum Clunie are back together to tackle the week’s jobs at Beechgrove Garden. Although George got a special picking of potatoes for his birthday in June, this is the time to lift the first crop from the vegetable plot and try out this year’s produce. Calum and George check on the brassicas that were planted in the club root-infected bed, testing varieties that are said to be resistant to the infection. George is back to work on the privet hedge that was given a severe pruning last year to encourage thicker growth, Calum gets round to placing plants known for their fragrance in his competition bed, and there are the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: A patient in Glasgow becomes violent, forcing crewmates Gregg and Bernadette to shelter in an ambulance. Unfortunately, this shocking incident is one that is becoming an everyday reality for paramedics across Scotland, with nearly 200 on-duty staff physically assaulted each year. In Dundee, paramedic Rebecca and technician Paige treat a patient who has suffered a potentially lethal drug overdose after taking a potent mix of MDMA and heroin. Rebecca and Paige must administer urgent treatment to save the patient’s life. Meanwhile, at the ambulance control centre, call handler Jackie takes 999 calls from two road traffic collisions - one in which a motorcyclist suffers a seizure, and another where concerns are raised about a baby. In both cases, Jackie has to keep calm under extraordinary pressure, organising an ambulance response while delivering important instructions to keep the patients safe. And in Aberdeen, the Special Operations Response Team is sent to help Allison, who has fallen at home and is now displaying the symptoms of a possible stroke. They also attend an expansive wildfire that has required a mass deployment of emergency service personnel.

programme.title: Chloe Ayling: My Unbelievable Kidnapping
programme.desc: Glamour model and kidnapping victim Chloe Ayling continues to look back at her terrifying ordeal orchestrated by Black Death. Now safely under the protection of the Italian authorities, she must give evidence in court against the man who enabled her escape from the international sex-trafficking gang – Lukasz Herba. But as the hearing starts and the evidence is laid out, a different picture begins to emerge of this particular suspect. Dazed from the shock of this discovery, Chloe returns home to the UK, finally free of the spectre of a gang she believed could continue to threaten her life. Whilst now free from one unimaginable ordeal, she’s immediately plunged into another as the Italian courts publicly release details of the case and the ongoing investigation to the world’s press. What she hoped to bury as an embarrassing nightmare soon ignites the interest of the global media. Now they know her name and discover where she lives.

programme.desc: With Beckham, Rooney, Ferdinand and Cole on the team, the 2006 World Cup was supposed to be England's moment. So why did the dream end in on-field agony and off-field acrimony?

programme.title: Golf: Scottish Open
programme.desc: Highlights from Sunday’s play as a stacked field featuring the world’s best players compete for the Genesis Scottish Open at The Renaissance Club in East Lothian. Masters Champion Rory McIlroy and World Number One Scottie Scheffler headline a stellar start list for the event which takes place a week before the 154th Open Championship. American Chris Gotterup is in great form as he looks to defend the title he won in 2025, with the home challengers including PGA Champion and 2020 Scottish Open winner Aaron Rai, 2024 winner Bob McIntyre, along with Tommy Fleetwood, Tyrrell Hatton, Marco Penge and the Fitzpatrick brothers.

programme.title: Kevin Bridges: In Search of the Beautiful Game
programme.desc: Kevin Bridges embarks on a journey to see if the beautiful game still exists. He meets Brazil football icon Cafu, Scottish legend John McGinn, Sao Paulo ultras, US football fans and many others.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: An expert witness uses fibre analysis to solve an execution-style murder, and after 26 years in prison, a man walks free when a forensic scientist links DNA to the real killer.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Viewers will be checking their change after watching this episode in Kent! David Harper meets a coin collector who reveals which rare 50 pence piece is worth 300 times its face value! John Wilson’s collection boasts 11,000 coins, including early medieval and Tudor hammered coins and the very first milled ones from the 18th century. Hoping to splash some cash of their own at Detling antiques fair are two teams of bargain hunters. In red are mum and daughter Nisha and dancer Adzi, with their expert Mark Stacey. Their opponents in blue are partners and musicians Kathy and Nardo. Nardo used to play drums in 1980s band Amazulu, and Kathy worked with some big recording artists of the era. They hope to compose a win with expert Kate Bliss, kicking off with a dolphin water feature, but four figures is too much to splash out on. The reds, meanwhile, are pinning their hopes on a set of cameo brooches, but Mark has doubts whether they will prove popular at auction. In Windsor, David hears auctioneer Harry Ballin’s estimates before the teams see their items go under the hammer – for a profit or a loss!

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team restore a ceremonial Chinese lion dance costume, a set of well-loved traditional beer pumps and two beautiful ceramic maquettes.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall, Jodie Kidd, Jamali Maddix and Suzi Perry take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another semi-final of the classic quiz where contenders return to the black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock to win a place in the grand final. The specialist subjects are the Norman Conquest, Borussia Dortmund, popes of the Renaissance and the film musicals of Alan Menken.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Sarah is a passionate livestock farmer and devoted to her Kunekune pigs. As she heads to the south east’s famous Edenbridge and Oxted Agricultural Show, she has high hopes of them walking away as rosette winners. Meanwhile, farming couple Frances and Simon are making their debut appearance at the show with their pedigree Dexter cattle, some of which play an important conservation role grazing in the South Downs.

programme.title: The Hidden World of Hospitality with Tom Kerridge
programme.desc: Tom explores a part of the industry close to his heart: the highly skilled and competitive world of fine dining. He meets chefs who, like him, are obsessed with the pursuit of culinary excellence. Is it possible to reach perfection when chefs are, by nature, never satisfied?

programme.title: Yellowstone: Wildest Winter to Blazing Summer
programme.desc: Patrick follows the grizzly bears that are taking a risk with the weather by leaving their winter dens early. Hungry wolves are struggling to bring down their elk prey in the unusually shallow snow. And for great grey owls, it is the iciness of the snow that is hampering their hunts. Yellowstone's winter is always one of the most brutal on the planet. But 2016 saw weather records broken, and the wildlife was forced to adapt to survive. Kate Humble gets to grips with the science behind this remarkable season, from understanding the importance of the snowpack's structure as the melt begins to uncovering why Yellowstone's unique geology poses problems for some grazers' teeth.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Chiddingstone Castle in Kent. He visits Anne Boleyn's family home, Hever Castle, and reveals what influenced her rise to power. Antiques experts Claire Rawle and Adam Partridge unearth unique antiques and collectables that reflect the local Kent character.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Eniola Aluko, Phil Daniels, Nikita Kanda and Danny Miller take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: If you could do just one thing to transform your health, what should it be? Zoe Ball, Roman Kemp and Clive Myrie show how one small change can make a big difference. From dancing yourself happier to eating mackerel for your heart, to soaking in a hot bath to help you sleep – they share the simple and surprising things we could all do to improve our lives. In postcard-perfect Rye in East Sussex, busy mum Sam is on a mission to supercharge her health after shedding the pounds with the help of weight-loss jabs. Clive Myrie has a simple but powerful idea for her next step – eating oily fish. And it turns out that adding this one food to your diet packs a serious health punch. Omega-3-rich heroes like mackerel, salmon and sardines won’t just help keep the weight off – they could sharpen mental focus, calm inflammation and even lower the risk of heart attacks and strokes.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: Bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents the first heat of the classic quiz where contenders face the famous black chair with the ultimate goal of becoming the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are 15th-century king Edward IV, the band Depeche Mode, the films of Yorgos Lanthimos and Roy Keane.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – as always, the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Three rowers take on a team of microbiologists in finding connections between apparently random clues. For example: Germany, HM Treasury, the Galactic Republic and the Duchy of Lancaster. What connects them?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The series kicks off with a match between students from Bristol and Imperial. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: Chris Packham embarks on an extraordinary journey through deep time to uncover how a creature as vast, complex and charismatic as the elephant came to be. From a tiny cell over four billion years ago to one of the planet’s most iconic giants, this is the surprising story of life's most radical transformation.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob accept a special invitation to fish the estate lake at Burghley House, which sits on the border of Cambridgeshire and Lincolnshire. Built in the 16th century by William Cecil, Elizabeth I’s lord high chancellor, Burghley House is home to some of the most majestic landscapes Paul and Bob have ever found themselves in. With a spectacular lake and stunning gardens, all designed by the iconic Capability Brown, Paul and Bob hope they can do the place justice - and net a decent catch.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Safe Haven
programme.desc: A young woman with a mysterious past lands in Southport, North Carolina, where her bond with a widower forces her to confront the dark secret that haunts her.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita Rani begins a four-part journey along England’s east coast, exploring the wildlife, landscapes and communities adapting to life on the edge of the sea. Her first stop is Northey Island in Essex, an internationally important refuge for threatened birds, including curlew, lapwing and dunlin. With rising sea levels putting increasing pressure on coastal habitats, Anita discovers an innovative conservation project using retired Thames barges to help protect the island’s future. She also meets the volunteers working to safeguard vulnerable ringed plover nests using a simple but effective solution. Anita also delves into the Countryfile archives to revisit some of the projects helping to create more space for nature to thrive.

They hope to compose a win with expert Kate Bliss, kicking off with a dolphin water feature, but four figures is too much to splash out on. programme.title: Yellowstone: Wildest Winter to Blazing Summer
programme.desc: Patrick follows the grizzly bears that are taking a risk with the weather by leaving their winter dens early. Hungry wolves are struggling to bring down their elk prey in the unusually shallow snow. And for great grey owls, it is the iciness of the snow that is hampering their hunts. Yellowstone's winter is always one of the most brutal on the planet. But 2016 saw weather records broken, and the wildlife was forced to adapt to survive. Kate Humble gets to grips with the science behind this remarkable season, from understanding the importance of the snowpack's structure as the melt begins to uncovering why Yellowstone's unique geology poses problems for some grazers' teeth.

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: If you could do just one thing to transform your health, what should it be? Zoe Ball, Roman Kemp and Clive Myrie show how one small change can make a big difference. From dancing yourself happier to eating mackerel for your heart, to soaking in a hot bath to help you sleep – they share the simple and surprising things we could all do to improve our lives. In postcard-perfect Rye in East Sussex, busy mum Sam is on a mission to supercharge her health after shedding the pounds with the help of weight-loss jabs. Clive Myrie has a simple but powerful idea for her next step – eating oily fish. And it turns out that adding this one food to your diet packs a serious health punch. Omega-3-rich heroes like mackerel, salmon and sardines won’t just help keep the weight off – they could sharpen mental focus, calm inflammation and even lower the risk of heart attacks and strokes.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita Rani begins a four-part journey along England’s east coast, exploring the wildlife, landscapes and communities adapting to life on the edge of the sea. Her first stop is Northey Island in Essex, an internationally important refuge for threatened birds, including curlew, lapwing and dunlin. With rising sea levels putting increasing pressure on coastal habitats, Anita discovers an innovative conservation project using retired Thames barges to help protect the island’s future. She also meets the volunteers working to safeguard vulnerable ringed plover nests using a simple but effective solution. Anita also delves into the Countryfile archives to revisit some of the projects helping to create more space for nature to thrive.

programme.title: Golf: Scottish Open
programme.desc: Highlights from Sunday’s play as a stacked field featuring the world’s best players compete for the Genesis Scottish Open at The Renaissance Club in East Lothian. programme.title: Cooking Buddies
programme.desc: Get your dancing shoes ready because Buddy and Conker get a call from Jaylen, a young salsa dancer who doesn’t stop moving! His mum is a professional salsa dancer, and Jaylen has learned all his moves from her, as he loves connecting with their Colombian roots through dancing. But there’s one thing that Jaylen loves even more... eggs! He asks Buddy to teach him an egg-cellent meal that he can make for his family. Buddy knows that if Jaylen loves dancing salsa, then he has to get him making salsa too, so he comes up with a cracking egg tortilla wrap filled with guacamole and zingy salsa. They learn to make their own tortilla dough in minutes, an omelette that sticks to the tortilla in the pan and colourful tomato salsa and creamy guacamole – cracking! Jaylen’s keen to get Buddy learning his kind of salsa too, so Buddy learns the basics of posture and footwork with the help of Jaylen… and some colourful socks! Join Buddy, Conker and Jaylen in this episode of Cooking Buddies that gets salsa onto your plate and into your step. You can get all of Buddy’s recipes, and loads more, at bbc.co.uk/food

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: The culinary journey this time takes Ainsley to North Africa - inspired by the memory of bustling souks and spices that awaken the senses, his first dish is a classic lamb, orange and prune Tagine. Shivi Ramoutar then goes to meet Jamal to learn how to make a traditional Algerian dish and create her own brunch dish of North African baked eggs before Ainsley is joined in his kitchen by former police officer-turned-presenter Rav Wilding, who has a delicious fish dish using some amazing spices for him. Ainsley's last dish is a one-pot wonder filled with the flavours of North Africa and just a little bit of spice - it's a rose harissa chicken and white bean stew with chermoula.
